entries.notes: Approved for Phase 1 commercial use. Effective license of the n8.0.1 build configured with --enable-gpl --enable-version3 --enable-libx264 --enable-libass --enable-libopus --enable-libwebp is GPL-2.0-or-later (the LGPL-2.1 core source becomes GPL-2.0+ once --enable-gpl pulls in GPL-licensed components; libx264 is GPL-2.0, libass is GPL-2.0+, libopus is BSD-3-Clause, libwebp is BSD-3-Clause). Determination authority: operator self-determination per FSF GPL FAQ citations; no outside counsel engaged. GPL-boundary holding: FfmpegMediaAssemblerAdapter invokes FFmpeg strictly as an external subprocess via child_process.spawn with no static/dynamic linking into Node.js, no C/C++ native addons, and communication via stdin/stdout pipes only. Per FSF GPL FAQ 'Mere Aggregation' and 'PipeLinking' clauses (URLs in licenseSource), subprocess + pipe invocation of a separately-distributed GPL program does not create a derivative work in the calling program, so the surrounding proprietary Node.js code is not contaminated by FFmpeg's GPL license. Distribution model: host-installed system binary on a separate medium from the Node.js application (apt/brew/downloaded system package; not bundled into the application's distribution archive). x264 patent exposure (MPEG-LA H.264 royalties): not a concern for the current deployment jurisdiction and use case. Host runtime build n8.0.1 continues to be evaluated at startup by apps/render-worker/src/cli/run-delivery-assembler.ts via FfmpegMediaAssemblerAdapter.getRuntimeComponents().
